description: Status page transparency upgrades is a cross-functional reliability initiative at Redwood Inference to make customer-facing availability reporting more precise, consistent, and actionable. The project improves (1) component granularity on the public status page (by product surface, region, and failure mode where appropriate), (2) standardized incident communications templates (initial investigation, identified, mitigation, monitoring, resolved, retro link), and (3) higher-quality post-incident summaries that are publishable quickly without leaking sensitive details. Scope includes defining a component taxonomy and ownership map (Hosted API, Streaming, Embeddings, Reranking, Console, Dedicated control-plane signals, key regions), mapping internal service health signals to public components, automating portions of status updates via incident tooling (incident-bot + runbooks), and updating the incident process to clarify roles (Incident Commander, Comms Lead, Scribe) and approval flow. Stakeholders: SRE leadership (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes), Infra leadership (Neha Kapoor, Irene Choi), Observability (Allison Grant), Product Console & Rollouts (Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes), Support/CS leadership (Dev Patel, Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim), and Docs/DevEx contributors for customer-facing language. Deliverables include Confluence standards/runbooks/templates, Linear execution plan, GitHub PRs across incident-bot/observability/config, and an enablement rollout (training + announcement). Constraints: avoid over-promising SLAs, prevent disclosure of customer-specific capacity issues, keep on-call burden low (templates + automation), and ensure consistency across Hosted/Dedicated/Private messaging. Proposed timeline (6–8 weeks): Week 1–2 taxonomy + signal mapping design; Week 3–5 implementation + templates + review; Week 6 staged rollout (internal dogfood → limited public rollout → full); Week 7–8 measurement (incident comms time-to-first-update, accuracy audits, support ticket deflection) and refinements.
